Core:
With inheritance this can lead to several if condition calls per one body/area entered signal through a script in comparison to one condition check in the core, this can be a lot less typing as well as less performance costly if done in core.
Since the functionality already exists on RayCast it can be a bit confusing why one collision detection node has it while the other one not.

I don't think add-on is a way for already existing node(?).
answers.workaround:
Yes, it can.

Check if node is parent in the body/area entered signal. But this has to be checked perhaps more often than it should, in case of inheritance let's say you have an inheritance tree like this:
Node A -> Node B -> Node C

If A has a method OnBodyEntered/OnAreaEntered and B and C override it while calling the base (A's) method to add more functionality then you will need 3 if conditions to check for the parent.

If you have deeper inheritance then you suddenly need an if condition per every node which inherits and extends the OnBodyEntered/OnAreaEntered.

So if you override the method and call the base you are calling the same condition multiple times per one body entered/area entered event, it's not just about typing the same condition several times but also about several exections of it.

This is very cumbersome and prone to mistakes.
